# Schema grounding and value linking for MQL generation — facts

> Source-anchored units about Schema grounding and value linking for MQL generation: 21 across 9 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-31 · 21 units · 9 sources · rights: quote -->

## Definitions

- [statement] Aggressive schema reduction is not universally beneficial. The Death of Schema Linking studies SQL generation with full schemas that fit the context window to avoid dropping required columns; IBM separately questions whether the smallest oracle-linked schema is optimal. Applying this caution to MQL is an inference, not a demonstrated MongoDB result. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.07702 · keywords: Schema grounding and value linking for MQL generation · also: https://research.ibm.com/publications/in-depth-analysis-of-llm-based-schema-linking

## Structure and components

- [statement] MongoDB grounding must preserve nested object and array paths, optional or missing fields, and BSON-relevant types. Flat field-name lists omit structure needed to interpret a request; MongoDB recommends representative documents alongside annotated schemas, while SAG induces structure from stored documents. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/natural-language-to-mongodb/ · keywords: Schema grounding and value linking for MQL generation · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.11201v3
- [statement] The mongodb-schema README documents optional structure-only inference through --no-values or storeValues:false. It also marks this repository archived and points to mongodb-js/devtools-shared/packages/mongodb-schema. Structure-only output omits the sampled value evidence that literal linking would otherwise use. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://github.com/mongodb-js/mongodb-schema · keywords: Schema grounding and value linking for MQL generation

## How it works

- [statement] Value linking binds a user phrase to both its exact stored representation and its schema location. Matching a plausible value at the wrong path or using the wrong stored casing can misground a predicate even when the field name exists. (high confidence) — https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/data-agents/querydata/firestore-mongodb-compatibility/context-sets-overview · keywords: Schema grounding and value linking for MQL generation · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.11201v3
- [statement] Resolve names and aliases before synthesizing precise filters when identity matters. Unblocked's MongoDB workshop explicitly orders schema discovery and identity resolution before synthesis; Google's value-linking example shows why a partial entity name needs a stored-value match. The workshop is architectural evidence, not a measured accuracy result. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/unblocked/document-query-engine · keywords: Schema grounding and value linking for MQL generation · also: https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/data-agents/querydata/firestore-mongodb-compatibility/context-sets-overview
- [statement] As an engineering inference, supplement schema descriptions with question-relevant stored-value evidence when a request uses aliases or partial entity names. MongoDB’s sample-document guidance supplies concrete examples, while Google’s Heathrow example demonstrates why a structurally valid field reference alone can still use the wrong literal. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/natural-language-to-mongodb/ · keywords: Schema grounding and value linking for MQL generation · also: https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/data-agents/querydata/firestore-mongodb-compatibility/context-sets-overview
- [statement] A separate schema-filtering stage is not universally beneficial: The Death of Schema Linking? reports SQL experiments where filtering removes required columns, and omits that stage when the schema fits the context window. This scopes claims that schema selection is always necessary; it does not show that database grounding or value evidence is unnecessary for MQL. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.07702 · keywords: Schema grounding and value linking for MQL generation

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] A sampled schema is incomplete evidence: Atlan documents that rare fields can be missed, and SAG exposes sparse paths only when observed. For MQL generation, treating every unobserved path as impossible therefore risks rejecting legitimate fields; this limitation follows from the sampling methods, rather than a guarantee about a particular generator. (medium confidence) — https://docs.atlan.com/apps/connectors/database/mongodb/onprem/faq/field-extraction-and-schema-inference · keywords: Schema grounding and value linking for MQL generation · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.11201v3
- [statement] An inferred MongoDB schema describes observed documents rather than a universal constraint. mongodb-schema records field occurrence probabilities and multiple observed types; DbSchema explains that sampling can miss rare fields. Grounding should retain uncertainty about missing paths and heterogeneous types. (high confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb-js/mongodb-schema · keywords: Schema grounding and value linking for MQL generation · also: https://dbschema.com/blog/mongodb/seeing-the-structure-of-a-schemaless-database/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Ground MQL generation in collection names, field types, and field descriptions. MongoDB recommends annotated language-native schemas; Cisco's agent demonstrates a YAML semantic model with collection descriptions and typed fields supplied before generation. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/natural-language-to-mongodb/ · keywords: Schema grounding and value linking for MQL generation · also: https://github.com/cisco-open/mongodb-nl-query-ai-agent
- [statement] Google QueryData documents developer-defined value-search queries that return a stored value, schema location, semantic concept type, and distance. Its Heathrow example maps the user phrase to London Heathrow at airports.name. This is documented for Firestore with MongoDB compatibility and is not evidence of an Atlas feature. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-26) — https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/data-agents/querydata/firestore-mongodb-compatibility/context-sets-overview · keywords: Schema grounding and value linking for MQL generation
- [statement] SAG, in the June 2026 paper revision, recursively samples documents into a path lattice with observed types and counts, represents dynamic maps with a <*> placeholder, and anchors question literals to witnesses recording exact stored forms and locations. Hard witnesses constrain binding; soft witnesses provide context. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2502.11201v3 · keywords: Schema grounding and value linking for MQL generation
- [statement] The text-to-mongo repository illustrates schema-conditioned training with typed semantic roles and enum values. It renames fields in both schema and query, and uses negative examples with nonexistent fields, to discourage field-name memorization. These are implementation techniques, not independent proof of production generalization. (low confidence) — https://github.com/jangel97/text-to-mongo/ · keywords: Schema grounding and value linking for MQL generation
- [statement] Schema context can include business meanings and synonyms in addition to technical field names. The engineering schema-card account recommends these annotations, and MongoDB recommends field comments to reduce ambiguity; neither establishes a single schema representation as best for every model. (medium confidence) — https://www.akshaydharphale.com/blog/text-to-query-nlq-mongodb-sql · keywords: Schema grounding and value linking for MQL generation · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/natural-language-to-mongodb/
- [statement] A domain-specific linking design can separate searchable terms from canonical entities: MongoDB's SNOMED architecture searches individual descriptions while returning the canonical concept, and Google's MQL value search returns a matched value with semantic context. This supports a linking pattern; the SNOMED example is not a general NL-to-MQL benchmark. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/solutions-library/healthcare-snomed-ct.md · keywords: Schema grounding and value linking for MQL generation · also: https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/data-agents/querydata/firestore-mongodb-compatibility/context-sets-overview
- [statement] Direct MQL guidance and implementations provide collection and field schemas alongside the question. MongoDB recommends annotated language-native types with comments that explain field meanings; Oza’s MongoDB study supplies collection names, field names, and types in the instruction input. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/natural-language-to-mongodb/ · keywords: Schema grounding and value linking for MQL generation · also: https://cs.rit.edu/~dataunitylab/uploads/publications/Oza2024.pdf
- [statement] Value linking must identify both the stored literal and its schema location. Google illustrates mapping “Heathrow” to “London Heathrow” in airports.name for MQL; StruG independently separates column grounding, value grounding, and column-value mapping in SQL. The SQL taxonomy is a transfer framework, not measured MQL evidence. (medium confidence) — https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/data-agents/querydata/firestore-mongodb-compatibility/context-sets-overview · keywords: Schema grounding and value linking for MQL generation · also: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.12773
- [statement] MongoDB recommends a few representative sample documents, serialized with BSON.EJSON.serialize(), and truncation of long fields, nested objects, and large arrays. Its suggestion of two or three documents is prompting guidance, not a guarantee of complete schema or value coverage. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/natural-language-to-mongodb/ · keywords: Schema grounding and value linking for MQL generation
- [statement] Google’s context sets for Firestore with MongoDB compatibility include MQL templates, reusable predicate facets, and developer-defined value searches. Value-search results can include the matched value, schema location, concept type, and distance; the documentation says this supports misspelling correction and value-type resolution. The documented feature is Preview and scoped to QueryData. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-26) — https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/data-agents/querydata/firestore-mongodb-compatibility/context-sets-overview · keywords: Schema grounding and value linking for MQL generation
- [statement] The EvoMQL preprint describes query-aware retrieval triggered by draft MQL queries to construct compact evidence contexts, resolve schema ambiguity, and ground nested paths to concrete values. This is direct MQL research evidence for an adaptive grounding approach, not independent proof that it outperforms static context in every deployment. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.13045 · keywords: Schema grounding and value linking for MQL generation
- [statement] Oza’s 2024 MongoDB capstone uses schemas and queries converted from WikiSQL and deliberately excludes complex join queries. Its schema-conditioned input design is direct MongoDB evidence, but the study does not establish coverage of native, deeply nested, polymorphic MongoDB documents or difficult value normalization. (low confidence) — https://cs.rit.edu/~dataunitylab/uploads/publications/Oza2024.pdf · keywords: Schema grounding and value linking for MQL generation
